thread:
sara: heads-up: we're seeing a sharp spike in container restarts on gpu-node-17, multiple pods OOMing then some hitting CUDA illegal memory access. cpu/mem metrics look normal, paging noise visible.

deepak: copying logs, rolling up what i have. suspect kernel misaligned address during pagewalk under load.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-0423. Severity: P2. Affected service: serving-runtime.

maya: i see repeated kernel messages in dmesg from gpu-node-17: ```[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at 0000:03:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed!
[ 12345.678902] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, PID 4123: GPF: UNKNOWN 0x00000000
[ 12345.678910] kernel: BUG: misaligned address in pagewalk at addr 0x7f9d3a1e0000```

sara: thanks. customer-eng -- any active customer reports?

customer-eng: one high-usage customer (acct-337) reported increased 5xx rate and some failed generation jobs. They're in EU, hitting dedicated pool.

ops_lead: put a cordon on gpu-node-17, draining low-priority pods. we should preserve crash logs/cores for triage.

maya: agreed. starting `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` and `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for non-critical pods. leaving dedicated serving pods until we snapshot logs.

deepak: capturing kernel oops + container core dumps: ```gcore -o /var/dumps/serving-runtime $(pidof runtime)``` also pulled /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and container stdout.

sara: is there an obvious regression? any rollout in last 2 hours?

maya: no infra rollout in last 6h. There was a model reload surge ~30m before spike — lots of KV cache fills. Could be stress on address translation under concurrent reloads.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF: oncall shift change in 20m. @deepak assigned as primary.

deepak: i'll take primary. plan: 1) keep node cordoned, 2) isolate reproducer on staging with same model reload pattern, 3) enable kernel pagewalk logging and run small repro, 4) if reproducible, hotpatch or kernel mitigations, else fallback to older driver/disable prefetch.

maya: quick mitigations we can do now: reduce aggressive prefetch and throttle concurrent reloads, enable prefix KV caching early to lower pagewalk churn. rolling config to dedicated pool via feature-flag.

sara: customer communication: send interim note that we're investigating GPU kernel errors causing job failures and that we've cordoned a node, some jobs rerouted; ETA 1h for root-cause investigation. @customer-eng can you send?

customer-eng: sending now. will include: affected region, estimated impacted customers, mitigation steps (cordon + drain + reroute), and ask for logs if they see specific job ids.

ops_lead: if we see repeat nodes, prepare batch cordon policy and shift traffic away from dedicated pool to hosted fallback model (lower perf but stable). throttle canary to 10% of requests.

deepak: repro attempt on staging: triggered concurrent reloads, running 5x load pattern. after ~18min, reproduced CUDA invalid memaccess with kernel backtrace. Extracted stack trace and coredump.

maya: posted stack trace to gist (link) and pinned to incident thread. Suspect race in kernel address space handling + nv driver edge case.

sara: classification: likely kernel+driver race causing misaligned pagewalk -> CUDA illegal access -> container crash -> node instability. Severity escalated if multiple nodes affected.

oncall-bot: NOTE: add-runbook-step "snapshot /proc/vmcore and dmesg on crash".

customer-eng: shared customer impact note: 12 jobs failed in last hour, 3 retried successfully after reroute, others require manual restart.

deepak: mitigation options weighed: 1) hotpatch kernel (risky mid-day), 2) rollback nv-driver to prior stable (tested on staging, helped), 3) throttle reloads and shift traffic to hosted. i recommend (2) + (3) as fastest safe path.

maya: prepping driver rollback for a small canary of nodes. will run on gpu-node-21 first, monitor 10m, then batch. will coordinate with infra.

sara: timeline: driver canary start T+30m, monitor T+40m, batch rollouts T+60-120m. keep customers updated.

oncall-bot: ACTION ADDED: rollback-nv-driver -> assigned to maya, deadline 52 minutes.

ops_lead: also collect perf counters to ensure rollback doesn't regress latency/cost.

deepak: attaching repro commands for eng-repro: ```python load_reloader.py --concurrency 40 --model large --reload-interval 5s``` and kernel logging flags we enabled: ```echo 8 > /proc/sys/kernel/printk; echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/panic_on_warn```

maya: starting canary rollback now on gpu-node-21. will keep node cordoned until validated.

sara: great. everyone please watch the incident channel. if more nodes show similar dmesg patterns, escalate to P1 and prepare customer-wide remediation plan. :rotating_light:

customer-eng: update sent to affected customers: we'll follow up with RCA once we confirm root cause.

deepak: preliminary triage notes saved to /incidents/5245003333/triage.md and artifacts uploaded to s3://incidents-dumps/5245003333/. retaining cores for 30d.

maya: canary rollback succeeded on gpu-node-21, no repeat after 25m of load. scheduling batch rollback starting in 15m.

sara: thanks team. closing initial triage; keeping thread open for RCA and postmortem.
